what_they_do: Prox builds an AI product specialist for manufacturers of complex physical equipment (AV/live production gear, powersports, construction and heavy equipment, HVAC, agricultural equipment, aerospace, medical devices, firearms). It reads a manufacturer's technical manuals, wiring schematics, and CAD files, then answers customer and technician questions with citations across the product page, dealer tablets, Slack/Teams, and support tools. It replaces the manual process of customers and field technicians digging through PDF manuals or waiting on senior staff, and doubles as a way to capture retiring specialists' knowledge and speed up new hire ramp-up.
vertical: Manufacturing / industrial technical support and field service
theme_fit_rationale: Prox's wedge is ingesting unstructured manufacturer documentation (manuals, wiring schematics, CAD files) that legacy support tooling can't read, then using that as a foothold into downstream workflows (pre-sales quoting, support, field service, onboarding) -- the core mechanic of Theme 5. Secondary fit with Theme 1 because a meaningful share of the source material and inputs are visual (wiring diagrams, CAD, technician-submitted field videos) in industries (construction, manufacturing) that Theme 1 explicitly calls out.
